business_scope.primary_industry_name: Export Distribution of Pre-Packaged Spicy Tallow Hotpot Base Bricks

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal civil-law jurisdiction; recommended registered seat in the Canton of Zug for crypto-valley and fintech banking synergies; for Stage 1 the country is treated as a unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Germanic civil-law tradition; Swiss Civil Code and Code of Obligations govern corporate and registration law; cantonal implementation of federal statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement (concluded 1990, amended by 2013 Protocol and 2019 MLI)
EFTA-China Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014)
EFTA Convention and Switzerland-EU bilateral agreements (continued through the 2021 UK-Swiss Trade Agreement)
WTO Membership and Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) applicable to low-risk food export flows

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220, Art. 620-763 on the Aktiengesellschaft, Art. 950-956 on company names); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0, Art. 2-8a, 9, 11); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV-FINMA, SR 955.033.0); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0, Art. 305bis/305ter); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (adopted 22 December 2023, in force as part of the 2024-2025 transparency package; creates a non-public central UBO register administered by the Federal Office of Justice); Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions ordinances implementing UN, EU and OFAC financial sanctions
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (statutory central UBO register is non-public; access is limited to authorities and regulated financial/AML obligees under Art. 56a AMLA; nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the Swiss-resident director, the auditor, and the account-holding bank; there is no public UBO portal)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate foreign shareholder(s) (e.g., People's Republic of China trading entity or Hong Kong broker/intermediate holding)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / Hong Kong Companies Registry / other foreign registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China has been an Apostille Convention party since 7 November 2023); where the issuing state is not an Apostille party: full Consular Legalization through the Swiss Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board/shareholders' resolution of the foreign founding shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Swiss AG, approval of the articles of association, capital contribution, and appointment of the first Swiss-resident director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of establishment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn German translation for submission to the cantonal Commercial Register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or national identity documents of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners along the full control chain (UBO piercing to the last natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (each certified copy individually authenticated)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate / police clearance certificate of each named UBO, director, and authorized signatory (Swiss Strafregisterauszug or validated foreign equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Office of Police (fedpol) or competent foreign criminal records authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-issued certificates, with certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of the foreign corporate shareholder and any intermediate holding vehicle (required for DTA relief and bank KYC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax administration of the shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign food production and export license of the hotpot base manufacturer (e.g., China Customs Export Food Producer Registration, health certificate, HACCP/ISO 22000 certificate, tallow product import-eligibility certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China / equivalent competent authority plus recognized certification body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and notarized translation; the Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) may additionally require the original health certificate routed through the competent cantonal food-safety laboratory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from a FINMA-licensed or SIC-member bank confirming the financial standing and business conduct of the ultimate beneficial owner and related entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial bank (e.g., in Hong Kong, Singapore, or UAE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-stamped original with signature verification; Hague Apostille not required if the bank is regulated in an equivalent jurisdiction, but consular legalization is obtained when requested by the receiving Swiss bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered office support documents: lease of the future Swiss registered seat or serviced-office contract with a licensed domiciliation fiduciary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Simple notarization sufficient where the document originates in Switzerland; no apostille or consular step required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory 100% screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, signatories, and trading counterparties against: (i) SECO consolidated Swiss sanctions lists (Embargo Act, SR 946.231), (ii) FINMA warning list, (iii) UN Security Council consolidated list, (iv) OFAC SDN list, (v) EU consolidated sanctions list as autonomously adopted, (vi) UK OFSI consolidated list, and (vii) the Swiss PEP dataset per Art. 2a AMLA and Annex 1 GwV-FINMA. Positive or ambiguous hits are escalated to the statutory auditor, the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO), and a suspicious transaction report (STR) is assessed under Art. 9 AMLA before any SWIFT TT or Letter of Credit is opened. UBO piercing requires identification of every natural person directly or indirectly holding 25% or more of capital or voting rights, plus de facto control and senior-management override; the central UBO register entry is filed with the Federal Office of Justice following incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), https://www.zefix.ch, operated jointly with the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) via the easymonitoring.ch and e-land.ch filing portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (Firma) must be composed of clearly spellable Latin-script words in at least one Swiss official language (German, French, or Italian); the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG/SA' must appear in a legible non-abbreviated combination; foreign or transliterated brand names (e.g., a trademarked hotpot brand in Pinyin or Chinese characters) are permitted only in Roman alphabet rendering, must not be misleading, and must be accompanied by a Swiss official-language descriptor of the actual business purpose; the name must be distinctive and must not falsely suggest a broader business scope (Art. 950-954 CO; Art. 62-63 Commercial Register Ordinance, HRegV).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Kreditbank, Sparkasse (FINMA banking license required)
Versicherung, Insurance, Assurance (FINMA insurance license required)
Treuhand, Fiduciary (only if the company itself operates a licensed fiduciary activity)

Swiss, Suisse, Schweizer, Helvetia (protected under the 2017 Swissness legislation, Art. 47-48 of the Trade Mark Protection Act; prior authorization required for the use of Swiss references on exported food products)
Holding, Group, Konzern (requires proof of a qualifying group structure and consolidated substance)
International, Global, World (requires demonstrable multinational business activity at the time of registration)
Names containing intergovernmental designations (EU, UN, WTO, OPEC) or federal/cantonal/communal coats of arms
Bundes-, Eidgenössisch, Verband, Stiftung (suggesting state character, a foundation form, or an association form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit a formal name pre-clearance enquiry (Firmenvorprüfung) to the target cantonal Commercial Register five business days before notarization. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file written legal arguments with the cantonal Register within 30 days of the refusal; a maintained refusal is appealable before the Cantonal Administrative Court (e.g., Verwaltungsgericht of the Canton of Zug) under cantonal administrative procedure law, and thereafter to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht, Lausanne) within 30 days. In parallel, a modified name (adding a distinctive element, geographical descriptor, or alternative legal-form rendering) may be submitted to the same registry without losing the earliest filing slot. Once pre-cleared, the name reservation is normally valid for 90 days and may be extended for one additional 90-day period if the notarial deed has been executed but registration is still pending; unused reservations lapse and the name returns to the public pool.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or PO Box address is not permissible as the statutory registered seat of an export trading AG. The company must maintain a real, physically accessible Swiss office in the canton of registration where corporate records, board minutes, and accounting books are kept; at least one director with individual signatory authority must be resident in Switzerland (Art. 621 and Art. 718 CO). A serviced office or licensed fiduciary domiciliation address is accepted if the provider can physically receive mail, retain minutes, and make the premises available for inspection; remote board meetings are permitted but do not substitute for the registered substance requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low aggregate risk. The cantonal Commercial Register performs spot verifications at incorporation and on material amendments (estimated probability below 5%). The cantonal food-safety authority (Lebensmittelkontrolle) and customs/VAT authorities (BAZG/ESTV) conduct unannounced inspections of food-export traders more frequently, with an estimated annual on-site inspection probability of 15-25% for a low-risk packaged seasoning wholesaler; scrutiny increases where tallow-based products are imported from non-EU/non-Swiss approved establishments and where the country of production is not on the FSVO positive lists.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial certification of the articles of incorporation (Art. 640 CO) including drafting, minutes, and verification of the statutory minimum capital payment (CHF 100,000 minimum capital; at least CHF 50,000 paid in)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary public office (e.g., Notariat Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff ordinance (Gebührentarif des Notariats); market range CHF 2,500-5,000 depending on articles complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal Commercial Register entry fee (Handelsregister-Eintragung of the new AG)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Commercial Register Office / cantonal Commercial Register of the selected canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ordinance on Commercial Register Fees (GebV-HReg); CHF 600-1,200 depending on share capital and number of registrable facts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ZEFIX name pre-clearance (Firmenvorprüfung) and conflict check
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal register fee schedule for name pre-check; typically CHF 80-150 per proposed name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of 7-9 origin documents (shareholder certificate, board resolution, passports, criminal records, food export licenses, tax residence certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Authentication Office / Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (apostille) and Swiss Embassy or Consulate (consular legalization where required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee of CHF 50-75 per document; consular legalization CHF 100-150 per document; certified German translation CHF 100-250 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, control-chain piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, and AML compliance opinion by a licensed fiduciary or external AML officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External licensed AML/CFT compliance advisor / fiduciary (Treuhandgesellschaft)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 250-400 per screened natural person plus one-year database subscription (World-Check, Dow Jones or equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss-resident statutory director and registered-office domiciliation service (first calendar year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate governance and domiciliation provider in the Canton of Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fiduciary market rate CHF 5,000-12,000 depending on transaction volume and regulatory workload; includes physical office, mail handling, board meeting facilities, and official correspondence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration as a Food Business Operator under Art. 65 of the Federal Act on Foodstuffs and Utility Articles (LAl) at the cantonal food safety office, including FSVO/BLV notification for imported fat-based seasoning cubes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal food-safety authority / Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal food business registration fee (CHF 100-400) plus FSVO/import-control assessment for third-country food products containing animal fat

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOG)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory SHAB tariff based on text length; CHF 90-170 for a standard incorporation announcement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial bank KYC and UBO attestation package for SWIFT TT and Letter of Credit routing (two FINMA-licensed banks, one in Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank account opening and due-diligence documentation fee under the Swiss Banking Self-Regulation Agreement (VSB 20); market benchmark CHF 1,200-2,000; includes sanction screening implementation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: VAT (MWST) registration, commercial register extracts, and certified translations of ancillary documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) / cantonal registry / sworn translation services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: VAT registration is free of charge; register extract tariff CHF 20-60 per extract; certified translation CHF 60-120 per page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Articles 620–763 (stock corporation), in particular Arts. 626, 635, 640 and 716b; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV, SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Registre du commerce du canton de Zoug), under cantonal authority and federal supervision of the Swiss Federal Office for Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authenticated (notarized) Declaration for Commercial Register Entry of an Aktiengesellschaft (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister) together with certified Articles of Association (Statuten).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked Swiss corporate account or confirmed in writing by a licensed audit firm before registration; in-kind contributions (Sacheinlage) require a licensed auditor's special report filed with the commercial register office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF the Aktiengesellschaft to be formed in Zug, Switzerland, adopted unanimously by the directors at the constitutive meeting held this day. Upon review of the certified articles of association, the Board resolves: (1) to ratify subscription by the founding shareholders of all share capital, confirm receipt of the paid-up minimum capital on the blocked account, and approve the share issuance list; (2) to adopt the registered office at Zug and authorize execution of the commercial register declaration; (3) to appoint the acting directors and the chairperson, granting individual signature rights to the chairperson and joint signatory rights to listed officers; and (4) to delegate company registration, food-business licensing, and opening of bank accounts to the chairperson.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Canton Notary (Öffentlicher Notar / Office notarial du canton de Zoug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders prepare the German (or French/English) Articles of Association compliant with Art. 626 CO, specifying corporate name, seat (Zug), purpose including export distribution of pre-packaged foodstuffs, share capital, and board organization. The notary public authenticates the formation act, confirms the subscription of all shares, and the founders countersign the share issuance. Deliver one original notarized set for the commercial register file.
required_dossiers: Brief corporate purpose description aligned with ISIC 4638
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions the corporate purpose or capital clauses, amend the Statuten accordingly or issue an interpretative board note, then resubmit for re-authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Paid-Up Capital and Blocked Account Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank (corporate account desk) or licensed statutory auditor (zugelassene Revisionsstelle)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders transfer the minimum paid-up capital (at least CHF 50,000, ordinary shares) into a Swiss blocked corporate account opened in the name of the AG in formation; the bank issues an advance blocking confirmation releasing funds only after commercial register entry; alternatively a licensed auditor confirms the capital is at the company's free disposal. For in-kind contributions (e.g., warehouse inventory or seed capital equipment), obtain a Sacheinlage audit report.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) or audit confirmation
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account pre-registration, provide the notarized Statuten and founders' resolutions to satisfy bank KYC; if the capital proof is incomplete, top up funds and obtain a revised confirmation within the statutory 30-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Order for Registration with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized application for entry of the Aktiengesellschaft together with the Statuten, the blocking confirmation, the directors' declarations of signature authority, and the list of directors to the Handelsregisteramt. Registration is effected by official order; after entry the company acquires legal personality. Pay the cantonal filing fee by account or registered invoice; request a certified excerpt for licensing steps.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns a query order, cure deficiencies (e.g., missing translation, signature specimen) within ten days, or file a supplementing notarized declaration; a refused registration may be escalated to the cantonal supervisory commission for ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Operator Registration and Export Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Food Control Authority of Zug (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat) and Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV), Food Export Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the start of wholesale trade in prepackaged spicy tallow hotpot base via the cantonal food control portal or FSVO form, submit a simplified HACCP and traceability dossier, product labels with ingredient declarations, and the site description (dry storage at ambient temperature). Obtain the Food Business Operator registration number for customs and export licenses; for consignments containing tallow, obtain, if applicable, the animal by-product / export certificate from FSVO veterinary services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection authority classifies the operation as processing rather than distribution, upgrade the HACCP plan and apply for a processing-specific permit; if veterinary issues arise on tallow, obtain the FSVO hygiene certificate and, where required, the Swiss Food Import-Export declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Registration and Non-EIA Compliance Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug (Environmental Office of the Canton of Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a short environmental registration / exemption notice confirming the activity is limited to wholesale storage and dispatch of pre-packaged goods; confirm no processing line, no VOC use, and no industrial wastewater. Maintain records on waste handling of unsold product (VVEA) and prove, if requested, compliance with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) and Water Protection Ordinance limits for site stormwater. The EIA Order Annex 1 does not require a formal environmental impact report for this activity.
required_dossiers: Waste management agreement/proof of disposal contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental office treats the inventory as requiring waste-management authorization, obtain an operating plan approval under VVEA; if a neighboring-protection complaint arises, submit an acoustic/immission survey and implement mitigation measures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety Certification and Occupational Workplace Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Feuerpolizei & Gebäudeversicherung Zug (Fire Inspectorate / Building Insurance) and Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a building fire safety certificate for the warehouse (smoke alarms, fire extinguishers, escape routes), a structural load confirmation for pallet racking, and a workplace occupational safety acknowledgment per Suva directives. For packaged spice products, keep safety data sheets and storage and accident documentation; obtain the occupational clearance certificate before start of operations.
required_dossiers: Safety data sheets for pre-packaged ingredients
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clearance is denied or conditioned, implement the required fire-retardant, rack-load or ventilation measures, then obtain a reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Food Control Authority of Zug (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat) in conjunction with the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV) and the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (BAZG) for export controls
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Registration and Export Foodstuff Permit (Unternehmensregistrierung nach Art. 77 Lebensmittelgesetz / Article 77 Foodstuffs Act)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU), Section Environmental Assessment; cantonal execution by Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal EIA under Annex I of the EIA Ordinance (UVPV/EIE) for pure wholesale storage and distribution of pre-packaged goods; environmental registration only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater; compliance with Clean Air Ordinance LRV (VOC ≤ 20 mg C/m³ general threshold where applicable), avoidance of food waste via VVEA waste management obligations, and sealed drainage/retention requirements for site stormwater; noise compliance at parcel boundary per LSV/OPB.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Zug fire inspectorate and building insurance, structural load inspection for pallet racking, workplace clearance by Suva (accident insurance), plus hazardous substance documentation for spice and fat components; occupational hygiene acknowledgment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), VAT Domain; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; electronic filing via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration 'eService' and Secure Electronic Data Interchange (SUKE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is automatically registered in the Central Business Index (Zentraler Unternehmensindex) and obtains a Swiss Business Identifier (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, UID) upon commercial registry entry. A foreign enterprise carrying on taxable supplies in Switzerland or receiving supplies that shift VAT liability must obtain a Swiss VAT number by filing the Swiss VAT registration application through the ESTV portal before the VAT obligation arises; if a UID is not yet held, the registration process simultaneously allocates one. Registration threshold: CHF 100,000 in annual non-exempt turnover from taxable supplies. For foreign businesses not resident in Switzerland, the competent cantonal authority may require a Swiss tax representative for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Swiss AG is a separate corporate taxpayer under corporate income tax and VAT, with resident unlimited tax liability on worldwide income plus preferential territorial treatment (exemption with progression) for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss VAT provides: (i) voluntary registration even below the CHF 100,000 threshold; (ii) VAT group taxation under Art. 12 VAT Act allowing controlled legal units to be treated as one taxable person; (iii) option to tax real estate letting transactions that are otherwise VAT-exempt. Switzerland maintains no US-type check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch entity elections under federal corporate income tax; hybrid mismatch implications are instead resolved via source and treaty rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in non-exempt annual global turnover received from supplies of goods and services (Art. 10 VAT Act); taxable purchases exceeding CHF 25,000 or entitlement to an input tax refund beyond the relevant threshold can also trigger deemed registration (Art. 11 VAT Act). Reduced rates: 2.6% for basic foodstuffs and 3.8% for hotel accommodation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has not mandated real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction controls (CTC); no central government tax clearance of invoices or digital stamping applies. Invoices may be issued electronically and must be kept audit-ready, but use of Swiss eBill, QR-bill, and PEPPOL BIS formats is voluntary unless agreed between the parties. Mandatory invoice content under Art. 26 VAT Act includes the supplier's identity, UID and VAT number, date, recipient, description, amount, and applicable VAT rate or exemption.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods physically transported out of Switzerland to the recipient or the recipient's agent qualifies for the 0% export VAT rate if the supplier transfers ownership and dispatch of the goods takes place abroad (Art. 23 para. 2 VAT Act), with export substantiated by customs documents or accepted digital customs clearance. Related services (loading, transport, processing, quality control and packaging) supplied to a non-Swiss recipient in direct connection with exported goods may also be zero-rated. In addition, certain services rendered to non-residents are not taxable in Switzerland if the economic benefit is effectively transferred outside Swiss territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / Export Customs Declaration lodged through the Swiss customs e-dec electronic system, required for physical export proof)
Bill of Lading or other transport evidence (CEFTA receipt, airway bill, truck manifest) proving goods left Swiss customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX confirmation that payment was received from a non-Swiss buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV scrutinizes zero-rating claims transaction-by-transaction against customs export records, transport documentation, payment flows and counterparty substance. For insufficient or fraudulent substantiation, the 0% rate is retrospectively disallowed and the VAT shortfall is assessed with default interest. Deliberate evasion or obtaining of unjustified zero-rating triggers criminal tax proceedings and a fine of up to three times the VAT shortfall under Swiss VAT criminal provisions (Art. 103 ff. VAT Act). Records must be retained for six years, and false export declarations may also expose the company to customs penalties and director liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully convertible currency regime with no exchange controls on either current or capital account transactions. The Swiss franc (CHF) may be freely converted, and there are no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance is subject solely to Swiss withholding tax of 35% on dividends and similar distributions, which may be reduced or refunded under applicable double taxation treaties. No prior exchange control approval is required for cross-border fund movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation requiring export receipts to be surrendered to the central bank or converted into Swiss francs. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in any convertible foreign currency, held in Swiss or foreign bank accounts, and used for trade payments, hedging, or reinvestment at the exporter's discretion. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%; statutory timeline: not applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for core treasury functions. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) generally cannot provide commercial bank account services to a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft without holding a Swiss banking licence or a FINMA-licensed fintech licence. Unlicensed foreign EMIs may legally partner with Swiss banks for payment initiation and e-money wallets, but they are not a substitute for regulated corporate bank accounts, and their use raises AML, counterparty, and substance concerns. A Swiss licensed fintech or a fully regulated Swiss bank is the compliant route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money laundering law does not impose a strict statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in a bank branch. FINMA-recognised video-identification procedures are permitted for natural persons, and many banks offer remote onboarding for corporate clients using electronic signatures. However, tier-1 commercial banks typically require at least one authorised director or beneficial owner to attend an interview (physical or virtual) and present certified corporate documents and passport copies. Fully remote account opening is possible only where the bank's due diligence policy adopts video/online verification for low-risk and standard wholesale clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) cannot be established due to complex ownership chain or missing personal identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register extract showing full shareholding chain, a signed UBO declaration (Form K, FINMA-compliant), passports of all natural-person shareholders, board resolution approving account opening, and organisational chart with ownership percentages.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flows or counterparties display mismatches between invoices and payment beneficiaries, or originate from high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts, proforma invoices, packing lists, bills of lading / waybills, customs declarations, tax invoices, bank statements of suppliers, and a written explanation of the distribution model with evidence of physical movement of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company is newly formed with a low equity base and no trading history, raising potential shell-company or business-purpose concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, financial projections, physical office lease or registered-office agreement, statutory auditor confirmation (if applicable), professional advisory engagement letter, and evidence of inbound capital remittance from shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are present in the ownership or management, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full PEP declaration, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, independent credit/financial reference from a regulated bank, tax clearance from the Swiss tax administration, and audited or externally reviewed financial statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires a SWIFT MT103 or equivalent covering credit transfer from the investing shareholder's bank, clearly citing a valid purpose code such as 'GFOR' (direct investment) or 'SUPP' (loan extended by parent) in the transaction description. The funds must be received into the Swiss entity's designated account at a regulated bank and settled via SIX Interbank Clearing (SIC) in CHF or through Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) for eligible FX transactions. Compliance verification must include confirmation that the transferor is the registered shareholder or lender, the contractual basis for the capital injection (equity subscription agreement, shareholder loan agreement), and evidence of commercial reasonableness. Anti-money-laundering checks require matching the SWIFT sender reference against the bank's approved KYC file and maintaining records of the inward remittance advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed predominantly over SWIFT MT103 for direct payments and via SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary credits (Letter of Credit) under UCP600 for secured trade transactions. For supplier payments to high-volume Chinese FMCG exporters, confirmation can be arranged through a confirming bank and settlement made under a commercial LC at sight or deferred payment basis. Urgent high-value CHF and EUR payments clear real-time through SIC; international USD payments flow via correspondent banking networks (e.g., USD CHIPS/ Fedwire). SWIFT MT103 must include invoice reference, purpose code ('PUR' for trade-related services or goods), and consistent beneficiary details matching the underlying commercial contract to avoid sanctions screening delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla Over-the-Counter FX Forwards with a licensed Swiss bank or foreign bank under ISDA or local master agreement
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exposure to restricted or thinly-traded currencies such as offshore CNY (CNH) or certain emerging market currencies
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to hedge combined FX and interest-rate risk on intercompany loans
FX Options (vanilla European-style or collars) for premium-defined protection against adverse CHF/CNY or CHF/USD movements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (federal and cantonal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and competent cantonal tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 June of the following calendar year for a 31 December fiscal year end; extension available upon written application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue interest (currently 3.5% p.a.), late-filing penalty up to CHF 3,000, and for deliberate tax evasion fines up to CHF 30,000; no administrative strike-off for tax noncompliance, but enforced recovery and board liability may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Return (quarterly or semi-annual depending on turnover)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after the end of each tax period; annual return option available only if taxable turnover is below CHF 100,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 5% p.a., administrative fine up to CHF 1,500 for late or incomplete submission, and VAT debt enforcement through liquidated offsets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the year following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution default interest, administrative penalty up to CHF 1,000, employer criminal liability for withholding violations, and compulsory debt collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and General Meeting Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and Annual General Meeting of Shareholders; retained for statutory audit and tax file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year-end, typically by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' personal liability for late or defective accounting; commercial registry may, upon shareholder complaint, initiate insolvency or ordinance proceedings for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit if the company is listed or if an AG exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets CHF 20 million; annual turnover CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees. If no threshold is exceeded, a limited audit is required unless all shareholders unanimously consent to a complete opt-out.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Swiss GAAP); IFRS is permissible for consolidated or listed entities; statutory accounts remain in CHF.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law imposes no separate annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing. The company must maintain an internal beneficial-owner register, verify identity upon share transfers, record changes in the share register (Aktienbuch) within 30 days, and retain documentation for the statutory retention period. No public UBO disclosure is required under Swiss law.
